YOUR SECTOR • Connection Bridge

Meet Connection Bridge

Know the themes. Meet the people. Explore several everyday situations.

Online conduct, tone and empathy

Explore gaming, school chats and everyday messages. Work out how the same click can land differently for different people.

Online conduct

How we behave through messages, posts, games and shared work.

Intent and impact

Intent is what you meant. Impact is what someone experiences. They can differ.

Tone and empathy

Context helps us interpret a message. Empathy means considering another person’s view without pretending to read their mind.

Jay

Quick with a joke in a gaming chat. Sometimes forgets who else can see it.

Ellis

Enjoys gaming and drama. A joke with friends can feel different in front of a crowd.

By the end, you will be able to:
  • Link actions to effects
  • Infer using context
  • Write a useful repair

Use the fictional details given. You never need to share a personal incident.

THINK DEEPER • Connection Bridge

Same words. Different meaning.

Use clues, consider perspectives and test your judgement.

→
Read the same words in two settings.

Inference and empathy: Use context to support a possible feeling. Separate what you observe from what you assume.

FICTIONAL CHAT
After Ellis scores a winner
Jay

Nice one.

Context

The team cheers and asks Ellis to play again.

FICTIONAL CHAT
After Mina loses the shared file
Jay

Nice one.

Context

Several people reply with laughing reactions. Mina stops typing.

Which visible detail changes how “Nice one” could be read?

How might Mina feel, and why? Give a possibility, not a diagnosis.

What can the chat NOT tell you about Mina?

TAKE ACTION • Connection Bridge

Repair the message

Turn your understanding into a practical response.

→
Draft a message that does something useful.

Repair: Own the action, reduce the harm and give the other person a choice.

NEW EVENT

The forwarded voice note

Ellis sends Jay a voice note about being nervous for an audition. Jay forwards it to two friends “to get advice”. Ellis asks him to delete it.

Practice draft · Jay → Ellis

Name what Jay did without blaming Ellis.

Give a concrete step to reduce further sharing.

Ask what support would help next.

Your sentences will appear together here.
Nothing is sent. Check how your message would land.
STRETCH • Connection Bridge

A public apology?

Take the optional Helpful Ripple challenge route.

Optional challenge · explain the tension, then defend a practical response.

TWO REASONABLE CONCERNS

Repair without a spotlight

Jay wants to apologise in the club chat so people stop requesting the voice note. Ellis says a public apology will make more people curious.

What deserves attention first?

Use ↑ and ↓ to order the cards. First = highest priority. Several orders may be defensible; your explanation matters.

  1. Reduce the spread

    Remove Jay’s copies and ask the two recipients not to forward them.

  2. Check Ellis’s wishes

    Ask what kind of correction or support he wants.

  3. Address the group

    Stop requests without retelling the private worry.

Explain how your first two steps balance practical repair and Ellis’s wishes.

Ripple City field guide

Key terms

Online conductHow we behave through messages, posts, games and shared work.
Intent and impactIntent is what you meant. Impact is what someone experiences. They can differ.
Tone and empathyContext helps us interpret a message. Empathy means considering another person’s view without pretending to read their mind.
IntentWhat someone meant or hoped would happen.
ImpactWhat another person actually experiences.
ToneThe attitude or feeling carried by words, punctuation and context.
EmpathyTrying to understand how another person may feel.
CyberbullyingRepeated or serious online behaviour intended to harm, humiliate or exclude.
RepairTaking responsibility and acting to reduce harm.
